s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pulmonary infection with systemic symptoms and possible CNS involvement
salient_findings: Progressively worsening chronic dry cough with shortness of breath
Night sweats and unintentional weight loss of 7 kg over two months
Cachexia with muscle wasting and poor oral hygiene including oral thrush
Dullness over right lower lung zone with reduced tactile vocal fremitus and fine basal crepitations
Pleural effusion and lung opacification on chest X-ray
Multiple brain lesions with diffusion restriction and peripheral nodular enhancement on MRI
key_facts: Homosexual with history of smoking and keeping cats as pets
Vital signs: Temperature 38.9°C, heart rate 128/min, respiratory rate 28/min, blood pressure 108/65 mmHg, oxygen saturation 88% on room air

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pulmonary symptoms, systemic symptoms, and possible CNS involvement

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: CNS lesions, immunocompromised patient, and chronic pulmonary symptoms

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: CNS lesions, immunocompromised patient, and possible pulmonary involvement

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia

shortlist.label: Nontuberculous mycobacterial infection
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic pulmonary symptoms, systemic symptoms, and possible CNS involvement

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including chronic dry cough, shortness of breath, night sweats, and unintentional weight loss, along with the radiographic findings of opacification in the right hemithorax with pleural effusion and non-enhancement within the right lower lobe lung parenchyma, are consistent with tuberculosis. The patient's low hemoglobin, elevated ESR, and CRP also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cryptococcosis
rejected.why: While the patient has some symptoms consistent with cryptococcosis, such as lethargy and fever, the radiographic findings and laboratory results are more consistent with tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: Toxoplasmosis typically presents with neurological symptoms, and while the patient has some neurological findings, the primary symptoms and radiographic findings are more consistent with tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia typically presents with more acute symptoms and is often associated with HIV/AIDS, which is not explicitly mentioned in the patient's history.

rejected.label: Nontuberculous mycobacterial infection
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms could be consistent with a nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, the radiographic findings and laboratory results are more consistent with tuberculosis.
